name: Wild angelica
grown_as: A native wild flower of damp meadows, woods and ditches, a strong pollinator plant. Short-lived perennial.
habit: A tall upright plant 1 to 2 m with a stout hollow stem, usually purplish with a whitish bloom and nearly hairless. Big umbels held high above a leafy base.

leaf.arrangement: Large leaves from the base; alternate up the stem
leaf.type: Compound, two or three times pinnate
leaf.leaflets: Oval to lance-shaped, 2 to 8 cm, all on short stalks or none; the end leaflet sometimes three-lobed; side leaflets often lopsided at the base
leaf.outline: The whole leaf broadly triangular, up to 60 cm
leaf.base: Leaflets rounded to wedge-shaped, often uneven
leaf.margin: Finely and sharply toothed all round each leaflet, teeth pointing forward
leaf.stalk: Long, channelled on the upper side. On the upper leaves the stalk base swells into a large inflated purplish pouch around the stem, which holds the young umbel.

flower.petals: Five tiny petals per flower, tips turned in
flower.behind: No bracts or one to three; a few bristle-like bracteoles
flower.carried: At the top of the stem and branches on long stalks, facing up; 15 to 40 downy rays

fruit: Oval flattened seeds 4 to 5 mm in pairs with broad thin papery wings at the edges, pale brown
seedling: Two long narrow seed leaves, then first true leaves three-lobed and toothed
winter: Dead hollow stems with seed umbels stand into winter; the plant is dormant as a root

leaf: leaf divided two or three times into oval pointed leaflets
fine sharp teeth all round each leaflet
an inflated pouch at the base of the stalk
bloom: large domed umbel of many rays
seed: oval flat seed with broad papery wings
seedling: first true leaf three-lobed and toothed
young: large divided leaves from the base on long channelled stalks
flower: tall purplish stem with a pale bloom
inflated pouches at the leaf bases
dormant: dead hollow stems standing, nothing green
old umbels with a few seeds left

look_alikes: Hogweed has rough hairy stems, large lobed leaflets and flat umbels with enlarged outer petals. Garden angelica (Angelica archangelica) has a green stem and greenish rounded umbels. Hemlock has purple blotches, not an even purple flush, and finely cut fern-like leaves.
